title: perf(canary): tune auto-detection thresholds and hysteresis to reduce false positives during bursty traffic
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Improve performance canary auto-detection by adding adaptive thresholds, hysteresis, and burst window handling to reduce false positive rollouts. No breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: Our perf canary detector has been producing false positive regressions during short bursty traffic patterns (observed on several customer canaries and internal perf-candidates). This resulted in unnecessary rollout halts and on-call pages. This PR adjusts the auto-detection logic to be more robust to bursts by: 1) introducing an adaptive threshold that scales with short-term variance, 2) adding hysteresis and minimum confirmation windows before surfacing a regression, and 3) treating short high-variance windows as a separate 'burst' state with reduced sensitivity.

What this change does: - Adds a configurable adaptive_threshold factor computed from rolling standard deviation over a short window. - Introduces hysteresis parameters (confirm_window, recover_window) to avoid flip-flopping. - Implements a burst detection path that requires sustained degradation outside of bursts before triggering a canary guard. - Exposes new config knobs in perf-canary config and Helm values for Dedicated/Private deployments. - Adds unit and integration tests + benchmark workloads to validate behavior under synthetic bursty traffic.

Checklist: - [x] Design reviewed with infra/observability (ENG-4231) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests (benchmark-lab) added - [x] Docs updated (perf-canary runbook) - [x] Config defaults chosen to be conservative to avoid missing real regressions

Testing: Ran benchmark-lab synthetic scenarios: 1) steady-state regression: detector still catches >10% latency regression within configured window. 2) bursty traffic (short spikes): false positives reduced by ~85% compared to previous detector. CI: linux-unit-tests, integration-canary, lint, benchmark-lab all passed (one integration flake rerun).

Rollout plan: - Deploy to canary tier only for 48h with increased telemetry. - If stable, promote to default canary behavior in 2 weeks. - If any customer-facing impact seen, immediate rollback to previous detector state using feature flag.

Related: ENG-4231, ENG-4297, SUP-8421. More context in docs/perf-canary.md.
